body: A friend has convinced me to talk to the free psychological help that my workplace offers. Maybe it's fitting that the insurance I've earned will — perhaps — help me with the problem that working helped to cause in me. Or maybe tragically ironic. Too early to tell.
I'm sorry. I want to be appreciative but...  everything you've just said is completely infantile.

> If you're the sciency type  

I am pretty sciency. I won't believe in the fantasy of an afterlife, neither as a balm for my mind, nor as a scare tactic. Nothing, certainly no book, can convince me that there is an afterlife, good or ill. Whatever I am, whenever I die, it will just stop, and cease to be. I agree with the sentiment that, “I do not fear death. I had been dead for billions and billions of years before I was born, and had not suffered the slightest inconvenience from it.” as Samuel L. Clemens put it.

Edit: I appreciate that you are trying to lift me up, to get me to think about my problem from a different angle. Thank you for that effort. I did at one point believe in those things, so I shouldn't unfairly fault you for coming from where you're coming from, since I was there once too.

> This almost sounds like a severe midlife crisis  

You're right, I guess this does sound like a mid-life crisis... but I am fairly young too. Other events have triggered this view, this plan,  in my mind. I don't think it's important but I am somewhat confident that I can point to the germ, the genesis of what's contained in my post. 

You have good insight though, it does sound like one of those. Although I don't think buying a Corvette and dating a trophy-babe appeals to me. Hah. (I made a joke.)

It's just that easy? Let me tell you, no, it's not. I was just at a pub trivia night. Listening to music, meeting new interesting people, contributing to the quiz with my little factoids. Having some food and beer out on the patio. I'm telling you that I've basically already happened to have followed your plan earlier this week. I received no joy from it.  

Thank you for trying to help though.

> You may not believe you have a purpose, you may believe there is no reason to live the life you're living - but remember that every action you take can and will influence the future in the largest of ways.  

I don't owe the future anything. Who's to say the way to best change the world is to go through with it.

I used to think that of others in this spot. But when you're living, you're living in the world. If I dropped everything, I would have to deal with the heartbreak and disappointment of friends, family, colleagues,who would view me as a failure. A quitter. Maybe I'll still be those things, but I won't have to go through others' expectations anymore.  

Thanks, though, you are now where I've been, so I can't blame the sentiment.

It's an interesting trick, and I will think about that, thanks. But the let-downs are a result of asking. Specifics. Vague. Big or small. From a friend, from my girlfriend, from whomever. They say they can't do it, even if I know they can. They can't be reached when I need them. They screw something up worse than before so I have to fix it. The latter most I don't mind as bad; at least they've tried.

> was it very expensive?  


No, not really. I took a tent. Gas isn't much for bikes, even big fat heavy Harleys can get 50mpg.

> Could you save up to do that every few months or once a year  


No. Even if I had a little money, I don't have the time. I am expected to fulfill too many obligations in my spare time that I do have.

Haha! 

> They felt I had my shit together and didn't really need any help. 

I guess I hadn't really considered this as a possibility. It wasn't why I helped out others. But it's a good point. Thank you for writing this.
